title: Pass 3 reduced model: dynamic thigmotropic contact coiling of a tendril around a cylindrical trellis support with Coulomb support friction and self-contact friction
scope_note: Pass 3 remediation of the Pass 2 audit item 'extend the 1D Kirchhoff rod solver to simulate dynamic contact-induced thigmotropic coiling around a cylindrical trellis support with self-contact friction'. Implemented as an overdamped discrete elastic rod (inextensible, bending-only, no material-frame twist) whose intrinsic curvature is zero until a touch signal arrives from a support contact and then rises toward kappa_contact pointing toward the support axis; the support is a rigid cylinder with penalty contact and exact overdamped Coulomb stick/slip; non-adjacent rod nodes closer than the rod diameter repel and obey the same Coulomb law on their relative tangential velocity; a post-coiling axial pull test measures the friction grip and is compared with the Euler-Eytelwein capstan gain exp(mu*Theta). Every number below carries a provenance tag. Values tagged 'assumption' are model inputs, not data; the only empirical anchors are Darwin's (1865) qualitative timings and support-size statements and the Pass 2 free-coil radius.

provenance_tags.literature: value read from a cited paper (approximate; could not be re-verified offline in Pass 3)
provenance_tags.derived: value computed from the SHA-256-pinned Pass 2 reference table tendril_perversion_intrinsic_curvature_reference.json
provenance_tags.assumption: order-of-magnitude modelling assumption with no direct tendril measurement
provenance_tags.prediction: model output with no empirical counterpart; reported for falsification, not validation

L_mm.source: length of the distal tendril segment engaged in contact coiling (Darwin 1865 Ch. IV: the distal part of the tendril wraps the support)

kappa_contact_mm_inv.source: saturating thigmotropic curvature of the contact-stimulated flank; set above the free-coil G-fiber curvature 0.65 mm^-1 (Pass 2 kappa0, Gerbode et al. 2012) so that 1/kappa_contact = 1.0 mm < R_support + a_rod = 1.25 mm and the coil squeezes the support (Darwin 1865: the tendril 'closely embraces' the stick). With kappa_contact = 0.65 the model loops loosely and holds no load for mu <= 0.6; see residual_remediation

R_support_mm.source: thin twig / trellis wire radius; Darwin 1865 notes tendrils grasp thin sticks and strings readily

a_rod_mm.source: tendril radius; cucumber tendril diameter ~0.5 mm (order of magnitude from Gerbode et al. 2012 Fig. 1 scale bars)

mu_support.source: Coulomb friction coefficient tendril-on-support; no measured plant-epidermis-on-wood value located offline (papillate tendril epidermis suggests high friction); swept over friction_sweep.mu_grid; in the model the loosely wrapped coil only holds load for mu >~ 0.5

zeta_mN_min_mm2.source: numerical drag of the implicit (backward-Euler) incremental potential; chosen so small that each macro step is quasi-static (elastic relaxation much faster than the thigmotropic ramp); the wrap clock is therefore set by tau_thigmo and v_signal, not by zeta

tau_thigmo_min.source: e-folding time of thigmotropic curvature after signal arrival; Jaffe & Galston (1968) report contact coiling of Pisum tendrils developing over tens of minutes

v_signal_mm_per_min.source: propagation speed of the touch signal along the tendril (Jaffe & Galston 1968 describe coiling spreading from the contact point along the tendril)

approach_angle_deg.source: angle between the straight tendril and the support axis at first touch; sets the helix pitch angle of the wrap

F_pull_max_mN.source: top of the quasi-static axial load ramp (20 levels, 2 macro steps each) applied to the released tendril base in the grip test; F_hold = load at which the wrapped segment slips 0.5 mm axially

slip_threshold_mm.source: axial slip of the wrapped segment that defines loss of grip

darwin_1865_contact_coiling.source: Darwin C (1865) J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 9:1-118, Ch. IV (Tendril-bearers), Passiflora gracilis and other species

first_visible_curvature_after_touch_s.note: Darwin reports a Passiflora gracilis tendril becoming visibly curved about 25 s after being touched (approximate reading; fastest case he recorded)

full_wrap_around_thin_support_min.note: Darwin describes tendrils forming a complete ring or wrap around a thin stick within minutes to about an hour after touch; range is a qualitative reading

support_size_statement.note: Darwin reports that tendrils fail to grasp supports that are too thick relative to their coil; the model reproduces this as a monotone decrease of wrap count with support radius (support_radius_sweep), but the threshold radius is a prediction

thigmotropic_direction.note: Darwin: tendrils curve toward the touched side (positive thigmotropism); modelled by pointing the intrinsic-curvature vector toward the support axis

expected_behaviour.note: holding load F_hold(mu) of the quasi-static ramp is non-decreasing in mu and vanishes for mu = 0; F_hold / (mu * sum N_i) < 1 because only part of the coil is in squeezing contact and the friction uses lagged normal forces
number of wraps N_wrap after 30 min reported for each R_support; the model winds loosely around supports thicker than 1/kappa_contact - a_rod, so no sharp enclosure threshold is predicted

near-circumferential approach gives a helix pitch below the rod diameter so successive turns touch; self-contact repulsion keeps the minimum non-adjacent node distance >= 2 a (1 - 0.15) and friction between turns limits inter-turn sliding

free_coil_radius_mm_obs.source: Pass 2 climbing_plant_species_table[0] (Cucumis sativus) coil_radius_mm_obs; used as the free-coil radius 1/kappa_contact ~ 1.5 mm reference

residual_remediation: No material-frame twist (Cosserat) degree of freedom: Gamma = C/B does not enter contact coiling; combine with the Pass 2 perversion solver in Pass 4
No circumnutation / support-search dynamics before first touch (rod is placed touching the support)
Friction coefficients and drag zeta are assumptions; the wrap time scale is calibrated to Darwin's qualitative window, so the time-to-wrap measurement is not an independent validation
Support is a rigid, smooth, infinitely long cylinder; no compliance, roughness or finite length

kappa_contact = 1.0 mm^-1 is an assumption chosen so the coil squeezes a 1.0 mm support; a contact-feedback growth law (curvature increasing until contact pressure saturates) would remove this hand-set value
